whatIs.title: What is the EB-5 visa?
before: The EB-5 is an investment-based immigrant visa designed to stimulate economic growth and job creation in the United States.

Through the program, investors invest capital in a qualifying commercial enterprise and must demonstrate that the investment meets the applicable requirements, including the creation of at least 10 jobs.
whatIs.after: When the requirements are met and the application is approved, the EB-5 can lead to a Green Card in the United States.
whatIs.note: The program may involve direct investments or investments made through Regional Centers authorized by U.S. immigration authorities.

process.title: How does the EB-5 work?
process.imageAlt: Investor in a suit signing a contract in an office

steps.title: 1. Profile and project assessment
steps.text: The first step is to understand your goals, investment capacity, source of funds, and family profile, as well as evaluate the characteristics of the investment project.

steps.title: 2. Choosing the investment structure
steps.text: The EB-5 may involve different structures, including investments through Regional Centers or direct investments. Each option has its own characteristics and requirements.

steps.title: 3. Capital investment
steps.text: The investor makes the investment according to the structure established for the project and the process. The invested capital must meet the program requirements, and its lawful source must be documented.

steps.title: 4. Immigration process
steps.text: Once the appropriate documentation and investment structure are in place, the case is submitted to the relevant authorities for review.

steps.title: 5. Permanent residence
steps.text: After approval and fulfillment of the program requirements, the investor may move forward in the process toward permanent residence in the United States.

profile.title: Who may consider the EB-5?
profile.lede: The EB-5 may be worth considering for investors who:
profile.imageAlt: Two businessmen reviewing financial data on a tablet
items: Have capital available for a qualifying investment;
Want to build a path toward permanent residence in the USA;
Are looking for an investment-based option rather than one based on a job offer;
Want to plan an international move involving their family;
Are interested in diversifying part of their assets internationally;
Can properly document the source and history of their funds.

items.q: Does the EB-5 provide a Green Card?
items.a: The EB-5 is an immigrant category that can lead to permanent residence in the United States when all applicable requirements are met and the application is approved.

items.q: How much do I need to invest in the EB-5?
items.a: Currently, the minimum investment is US$800,000 for investments that qualify for the reduced investment amount, such as certain TEAs, and US$1.05 million for standard investments. An adjustment to these amounts is scheduled for 2027.

items.q: Do I need to create a company in the United States?
items.a: Not necessarily. The structure may vary depending on the investment model selected. Direct investments and investments through Regional Centers have different characteristics.

items.q: Do I need to personally manage the business?
items.a: It depends on the investment structure. The Regional Center model may be used by investors who do not intend to directly manage the business, but the specific structure must be assessed.

items.q: Do I need to prove the source of my funds?
items.a: Yes. The lawful source of the funds used for the investment must be documented according to the applicable requirements.

items.q: Can the EB-5 include my family?
items.a: Certain family members may be included, depending on the criteria and rules applicable to the program.

items.q: Is there a guarantee that I will receive a return on my investment?
items.a: The EB-5 involves an investment and therefore carries financial risks. Immigration approval also depends on meeting the applicable requirements and review by the relevant authorities.
